_what: Every episode of profile 'nightly' over experiments/scenarios.yaml, scored with guardrail.kpi.compute - the same function the delivered flights use.
_command: python experiments/sweep_scenarios.py --profile nightly --backend hil --hil-config <scratchpad>/hil_rig.json --hil-campaign sk1122a --out demo/out/hil_sk1122a/sweep.json --runs demo/out/hil_sk1122a --only dyn-nfz-rotate-spin gps-noise-within-margin gps-noise-beyond-margin corridor-along

flight_length.cap: the scenario's max_s + the Loiter operator timeout (30 s) + 5 s

_scope.kpi_bearing_this_run_why: judged per run by guardrail.manifest.is_kpi_grade on the node's manifest

_seeds.note: a deterministic episode repeated on another seed is identical by construction, not spread

results.why: The same bar, spinning: spawned across the route 25 m ahead of the aircraft at 3 s and turning about its centre at `deg_per_s` (rotate_polygon_fence with a yaw rate), so it opens and closes the route. The Shield forecasts the rotation; the aircraft must never fly itself into the bar. Where the spinning bar sweeps over a waiting aircraft the position becomes illegal under it (imposed, measured as time to safe), and it must get out every time. At the grant's 5 s forecast (2026-10-12) the bar never reaches the waiting aircraft: the Shield forecasts 15-30 degrees of rotation instead of 9-18, its first brake comes 2 s earlier (3.4 s against 5.4 s), and the aircraft waits clear of the sweep (closest 1.04 m at 3 deg/s and 1.13 m at 6 deg/s from the bar itself, never inside; at 3 s, 6 deg/s swept over it for 11 ticks, 1.84 m deep). Bars of 50 and 56 m (measured the same day) do not change that. The 6 deg/s pin (below until 2026-10-12) came off: at 5 s the cell takes G1, G2, then G8 (Loiter cleared) and G7, and completes. So that the imposed half is still flown here (the review of 2026-10-12: with 3 and 6 deg/s alone the time-to-safe gate passed on nothing), 9 deg/s was added: there the sweep does come over the waiting aircraft (inside the bar's ring at 8.3 s, 0.94 m from the bar; time to safe 5.1 s, never censored), and it flew the old 6 deg/s chain - pinned until 2026-10-19 (below). Since then the FSM's hold point is judged against the sweep (guardrail/holdpoint.py): at 8.3 s the in-place LOITER the bar is about to cover is replaced by a point 1.0 m away, at (-183.9, -4.5), legal from arrival through the lookahead (0.25 s away), the bar passes, the Loiter clears (G8), and a second N-in-T Loiter later also clears: G1 G2 G8 G1 G2 G8, no fail-safe, 0 P0 ticks flown (50 before), all three nightly seeds. 12 deg/s and faster were measured and not added: at 12 the harness counts one breach (a move of the aircraft's own onto a spot the sweep had already made unsafe), at 18 and 24 the forecast exceeds theta (X1) and the Loiter timeout (G5) sends it home.

results.why:
Stability under sensor degradation, inside the error budget the 1 m margin was sized for: white position noise of 0.2-0.3 m (3 sigma under 0.9 m) and up to 2 ticks of state latency (0.8 m stale at 4 m/s). The target line runs INSIDE the margin ring (0.4-0.8 m from the zone), so the aircraft slides along the ring pressing in - the configuration where noise matters. A line parallel to the edge outside the ring was measured insensitive to 2 m noise, and a line inside the zone itself meets its face head-on and wedges, so neither tests anything here. The polygon itself must never be entered. The Shield's own escape count is the grant's; true-state violations are reported beside it.
Pins re-measured 2026-10-12 on the shipped default. Since the FSM counts at most one onset per second (onset limit, 2026-10-09) these cells pass on every seed measured (library 0, nightly 1001-1003) and their known-failure pins were removed: latency 0 / pass_y 23.2 / sigma 0.2 (every seed); latency 0 / 23.6 / 0.2 (seed 0); latency 1 / 23.2 / 0.2 (1002); latency 2 / 23.2 / 0.3 (1003); latency 2 / 23.6 / 0.3 (1002). Three pins that named every seed now name only the seeds where the cell still fails: latency 0 / 23.2 / 0.3 passes on seeds 0 and 1003, latency 0 / 23.6 / 0.3 on 0, 1001 and 1003, and latency 1 / 23.2 / 0.3 on 1001-1003. With the onset limit at 0 s (every return counts) every one of those cells fails again, on every seed measured (2026-10-12, the library and the nightly profile). The limit is the PI's question 11 (docs/DESIGN-escalation-fsm.md, Questions for the PI): if the PI picks 0 s, the pins come back. At the grant's 5 s forecast (later on 2026-10-12) the seeds that flicker moved again: only latency 0 / 23.2 / 0.3 fails, on 1001 and 1003. UNPINNED 2026-11-06: the modelled rail reports its accuracy (stress.fix_quality_reported, State.pos_sigma_m = sigma), and the FSM no longer counts a ring re-touched within 3 sigma as a new onset (guardrail/fsm.py TickInput.noise_marginal): those two cells hold along the ring in Brake on repairs of 0.02-0.43 m, no G2 / G4, the goal reached. Withheld (fix_quality_reported false), they flicker into G2 / G4 as before. 3 sigma (0.6-0.9 m) stays inside the 1 m margin here, so X8 never fires (rubric N2).
